analyst_view.overall: Early view: Dortmund have the league's best defence and are unbeaten, but they play at Arsenal in the Champions League five days earlier. Leverkusen, likely coming off a European game that week, have been inconsistent under Carles Martínez and concede often. Serhou Guirassy should be back from his thigh strain by then if his recovery goes to plan.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. Dortmund's league games are usually tight (23 goals in nine) while Leverkusen's are open (37 in nine), and the number sits between them. I stay with it.

corners.text: The site expects 9.6 corners. Leverkusen keep the ball for long spells and Dortmund are comfortable defending deep, as they did against Bayern, which tends to produce corners for the visitors. I lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I lean higher: Leverkusen's recent games have been card-heavy (eleven yellows in the derby, seven in an hour against Stuttgart) and this is a top-five meeting after a draining European week. Dortmund had three players booked against Elversberg.

shots.text: The site has 27.2 shots. Dortmund limit opponents well and do not need many shots themselves, and both sides may be tired after midweek, so I lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 on target. Leverkusen's loose defence gives Dortmund chances, while Dortmund's deep defending keeps Leverkusen's efforts from good areas to a minimum; these balance out, so I stay level.
